newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-DEPRESSING DAY IN THE COPA AMERICA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPRESSING DAY IN THE COPA AMERICA.

text.p: Two lackluster games, one played in an almost deserted stadium, underlined the fact Sunday that this year's Copa America soccer tournament is turning into a huge non-event.
The air in the high altitude venues is thin and atmosphere of a different kind was lacking as Bolivians found better things to do than watch a competition which has always appeared doomed to failure.
A mere 2,000 fans were scattered around a 32,000-capacity stadium in the attractive colonial city of Sucre to watch Uruguay beat also-rans Venezuela 2-0 in group B.
Even the hosts could only lure 15,000 fans to their 2-0 win over Peru in the same group.

Squeezed in between the region's World Cup qualifying games, which carry a far higher priority, the tournament has became at best a chance for coaches to test less experienced players, and at worst a severe headache.

Chile's Nelson Acosta seemed anything but disappointed after Friday's 2-0 defeat by Argentina in group A left his side as good as eliminated. He joined the chorus of criticism aimed at the timing of the competition.

The only teams who appear to be finding it useful are Brazil, who as champions qualify automatically for next year's World Cup and need as many games as they can get, and Venezuela, who are so far behind in the South American qualifiers that they cannot reach France.
Bolivia hardly helped their public relations cause when they imposed a media silence, which in turn led to local reporters boycotting their training sessions.
But as hosts they may have felt a moral obligation to field a full-strength team and found little difficulty in overcoming a youthful Peruvian side at 3,600 metres above sea level in the capital.

Goals by Marco Etcheverry and Julio Cesar Baldivieso either side of half time sunk an experimental Peru team that had Jose Reyna sent off for an awful tackle after just 15 minutes. The win allowed Bolivia to become the first team to clinch a quarter-final berth.
Uruguay, struggling in the World Cup and with a defeat by Peru behind them, overcame Venezuela with goals by Alvaro Recoba and Marcelo Saralegui.
Recoba's goal was one of the best of the tournament, as he burst through a group of defenders and slotted the ball under goalkeeper Rafael Dudamel.
With Sucre 2,700 metres above sea level, the last quarter of the match was played at walking pace.
Both games had moments of skill but neither ever looked like catching fire.

In Cochabamba, where group A matches are being played, Ecuador's players found themselves in the unaccustomed role of signing autographs. Dozens of fans watched their training session following their shock 2-0 win over Paraguay Saturday, which virtually guaranteed them a quarter-final place.
The win was especially sweet for Argentine-born striker Ariel Graziani, who scored the second goal.

"This is a tremendous moment, a kind of revenge after what happened to me in Argentina," he said, referring to a spell with Newell's Old Boys when he was only given a handful of chances in the first team.
Ecuador seemed an especially pleasant option for Cochabamba's fans as Argentina, who face Paraguay Monday, once again made little effort to endear themselves to the locals.
They have held most training sessions behind closed doors and their players have been the only ones not to venture out into the city.
